title: DNA damage accumulation and declining repair capacity
bottleneck: Genomic instability is a primary hallmark of aging: DNA lesions accumulate as repair pathways (base excision, homologous recombination) lose efficiency. Yet boosting repair is hard to do safely, since hyperactive repair can itself cause mutations, and the field cannot yet measure an individual's DNA damage burden in vivo.
why_it_blocks: DNA damage underlies cancer, cellular senescence, and stem cell exhaustion simultaneously. Without a way to quantify and restore repair capacity, the most fundamental aging lesion stays untreatable.
current_state: PARP inhibitors exploit repair defects in cancer but are not anti-aging drugs. NAD+-dependent repair (sirtuins) is targeted by precursors with unproven human benefit. No therapy restores youthful repair fidelity. Single-cell sequencing now maps mutation burden across tissues, revealing striking variation, but no intervention has been shown to lower somatic mutation accumulation in humans.
